peers.name: animation-performance
peers.description: Keep web animations inside the frame budget — animate composite-only properties, keep motion off the main thread when the page is busy, and find the cause when an animation drops frames. Use when an animation is janky, choppy, stutters, or drops frames; when choosing which property to animate; when deciding between CSS and JS animation on performance grounds; or when reaching for `will-change` or GPU layers. For choosing easing, duration, or whether to animate at all use animate; for reviewing motion as a whole use review-animations.

peers.name: emil-design-eng
peers.description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy for UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great. Use when building or reviewing a UI component's interactions and polish (press and hover states, popover origin, tooltip timing, transitions vs keyframes, clip-path techniques, drag details) and no narrower skill fits.

peers.name: review-animations
peers.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

peers.name: apple-design
peers.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

en.tagline: Rules for drag, swipe and sheet gestures
en.summary: Guidance for building gestures that users drag, swipe, fling, or hold. It splits each gesture into a tracking phase, where the element follows the pointer exactly, and a release phase, where a spring finishes the motion. It also covers when to use Vaul for sheets and how to keep gestures interruptible.
problem: Gestures built with fixed timing, or with React state updated on every move, often feel laggy, detached from the finger, or jumpy on release. A sheet or card that cannot be caught mid-animation also feels broken.

With this skill, the element tracks the pointer 1:1 through motion values or direct transform writes. On release, a spring starts from the gesture's velocity, so the motion continues naturally. Dismissal depends on both distance and velocity, and the animation can be interrupted at any point.
unfit: Plain button clicks or static layouts with no dragging
Animations not connected to user input
steps: Check first whether a library covers the interaction; for bottom sheets and drawers, the skill recommends Vaul.
While the pointer is down, drive position from a useMotionValue or direct transform writes, with no spring or transition.
Past a boundary, use dragElastic to apply rubber-band resistance instead of stopping dead.
On release, finish the motion with a spring seeded by the release velocity, or with a CSS transition for CSS-only components.
Dismiss when the drag passes about 40% to 50% of the travel or when the velocity is high, and snap back quickly otherwise.
For anything a gesture can touch, use only transitions and springs, not @keyframes, so the user can catch it mid-animation; then test on a real phone.

zh.tagline: 拖拽、滑动和底部面板手势的实现规则
zh.summary: 为用户可拖拽、滑动、甩动或长按的交互提供构建指南。它把每个手势分为两个阶段：手指按下时，元素严格跟随指针；松开后，由弹簧动画完成后续运动。内容还包括何时用 Vaul 实现底部面板，以及如何让手势可以中途打断。
problem: 用固定时长，或每次移动都更新 React 状态的方式做手势，常见问题是卡顿、与手指脱节，或松手时跳动。无法在动画中途抓住的面板或卡片也会让人觉得有问题。
使用这套规则后，元素通过 useMotionValue 或直接写入 transform 与指针保持 1:1 对应。松手时，弹簧从手势释放速度开始运动，衔接更自然。关闭判断同时参考距离和速度，动画也可以在任何时刻被打断。
fit: 可滑动关闭的提示或卡片
拖拽排序、下拉刷新或长按确认
unfit: 普通按钮点击，或没有拖拽的静态布局
与用户输入无关的动画
steps: 先判断现有库能否覆盖这种交互；底部面板和抽屉默认推荐使用 Vaul。
指针按下时，用 useMotionValue 或直接写入 transform 驱动位置，不使用弹簧或过渡。
越过边界时，用 dragElastic 做橡皮筋式阻尼，而不是直接停住。
松手后，用带有释放速度的弹簧完成运动；纯 CSS 组件则使用 CSS 过渡。
拖动超过约 40% 到 50% 的距离，或速度足够快时关闭，否则快速回弹。
手势可能影响的元素只使用过渡和弹簧，不用 @keyframes，以便中途打断；最后在真实手机上测试。
